semanticReview.method: Manual comparison with the Taiwan Ministry Hanyu Pinyin scheme and Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary

findings.supports: The scheme writes 韻母ㄦ as er and writes ㄦ as r when it is used as a coda.
The Ministry dictionary defines 兒化音 as a suffix that joins to the prior syllable and makes a retroflex final.
The dictionary registers 二 as èr and the number two.
The dictionary registers 耳 as ěr and the ear.
The dictionary registers 兒 as ér, child/son, and also describes the suffix use.
The dictionary registers 而 as a separate character pronounced ér with its own grammatical uses.

limitations: No unsupported articulatory instructions or broad claims about dialect frequency of erhua are retained.
